saml.description: When Allow IDP-Initiated Logins is enabled on a SAML source, authentik allows IdP-initiated logins even though the request is not verified; the documentation explicitly warns this may constitute a security risk.
saml.note: Do not report successful unsolicited SAML login as an implementation bug if this option is intentionally enabled.

saml.description: Using email address as SAML NameID is discouraged because users are free to change email addresses by default.
saml.note: Identity changes or merges driven by mutable email-based identifiers may be expected configuration behavior, not a broker flaw.

saml.description: When NameID policy is EmailAddress, the identifier is based on the user's email, which authentik warns may be user-changeable.
saml.note: Identity drift or merge behavior tied to email changes may be by design if email-based NameID is chosen.

saml.description: Applications with no bindings defined are accessible to all users by default.
saml.note: Broad access in an unbound application is by design and should not be flagged as authorization escalation caused by SAML.

saml.description: Allowing IdP-initiated logins on a SAML source is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified and could authenticate a user without interaction.
saml.note: Successful IdP-initiated login under this setting should not be treated as an implementation bug; it is an explicitly documented risky configuration.

saml.description: When a flow is suspended for an external source and the resume timeout is exceeded, authentik restarts the suspended flow from the beginning.
saml.note: Delayed returns from the upstream SAML IdP can legitimately restart the flow and should not be misclassified as session confusion.

saml.constraint: SAML login testing against authentik as SP MUST use the ACS endpoint /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with HTTP POST form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState. SP-initiated flows require a matching AuthnRequest/InResponseTo, so the executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState; sending a fabricated unsolicited POST without flow initiation can fail for setup reasons unrelated to the security property under test.
saml.source: users-sources/sources/protocols/saml/index.md; Required rule for SAML ACS extraction

saml.constraint: For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-security testing, authentik documentation states the SAML source supports signed requests, but the docs do NOT expose API fields here for enforcing signature validation options. The fuzzer MUST treat missing admin configuration endpoints as a documentation limitation and only test the documented ACS behavior; do NOT infer undocumented toggles or assume insecure defaults from absent docs alone.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified and could be used to authenticate a user without interaction. For valid I3/I1 testing, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated ACS tests from IdP-initiated behavior; if IdP-initiated logins are enabled in the target instance, successful unsolicited assertions may be by design rather than a signature/session-binding bypass.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit Issuer/Entity ID for the upstream IdP. If the source is not configured with the expected IdP entity ID, issuer-mismatch results are uninterpretable because the test cannot distinguish missing trust configuration from failed issuer enforcement.

For I2 replay tests (saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay), include a CONTROL login using a fresh valid assertion in the same environment. Without a control, a failed second login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML source setup, expired suspended flow state, or missing RelayState/InResponseTo correlation.

The Source stage resume timeout can cause a suspended flow to restart from the beginning after return from the configured source. For I3 flow-coherence tests involving embedded SAML source execution, the fuzzer MUST keep the SAML round-trip within the configured resume timeout; otherwise failures may be due to flow restart rather than session-binding or atomicity bugs.

For I4 principal-binding tests, NameID format selection materially changes the identifier authentik receives. Persistent maps to a hashed ID, transient maps to session ID, emailAddress maps to email, and some formats fall back to persistent identifiers when attributes are absent. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins; changing NameID format between trials changes the upstream identifier semantics and can create false collision or false separation results.

Email-based NameID is documented as mutable by default because users may change email addresses. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT treat merges caused by intentionally email-based identity selection as proof of a broker bug unless the deployment explicitly relies on immutable identifiers. Prefer persistent NameID when testing stable principal binding.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, authentik documentation indicates SAML source property mappings can map both NameID and attributes into authentik user properties, but the exact matching/merge rules are not specified here. The fuzzer SHOULD test both NameID-vs-email disagreement cases and interpret any merge cautiously unless corroborated by returned identity details; do not assume binding is by NameID only or by email only from these docs.

For I5 tests involving SAML attributes and group/type confusion, LDAP/other source mapping docs note that some imported fields may remain arrays unless flattened. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test string-vs-list forms for mapped attributes/groups because authentik may preserve source data types through property mappings rather than normalizing them to strings.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature-integrity tests, target authentik as a SAML Source (authentik acting as SP) via POST to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. The docs state authentik supports signed requests and that the ACS consumes assertions sent from the IdP. Tests must use the ACS endpoint, not provider SSO endpoints, because the provider endpoints are for authentik acting as IdP to downstream SPs.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo semantics. The ACS consumes assertions in an SP-initiated flow, and the SAML source docs define the ACS URL as /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. Send the forged SAMLResponse only after starting the flow indicated by metadata/SSO configuration.

For I1 issuer-validation tests (saml_issuer_mismatch), configure the SAML source with an explicit upstream Issuer/Entity ID and then vary the assertion Issuer. The docs expose Issuer/Entity ID as a source configuration field; if it is not configured correctly, issuer-mismatch results are ambiguous because the test may be exercising incomplete setup rather than issuer enforcement.

For I1 default-risk testing, authentik documents 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' as a security risk because the request is not verified and could be used to authenticate a user without interaction. Do not treat successful IdP-initiated login as a proof-integrity bug if that option was intentionally enabled; record it as insecure-by-configuration unless the same behavior occurs with the option disabled.

For I2 replay tests, use SAML-specific replay patterns only. The attack catalog's JWT replay expectations do not apply here. Test repeated submission of the same SAML assertion ID and OneTimeUse assertions against /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/.

For I3 MFA-bypass testing, authentik flows are stage-based and alternate authentication paths can differ. The valid SAML-only test is: verify the normal authentik authentication flow requires MFA for the victim, then authenticate through the SAML source path with the same bound identity. A finding is only meaningful if the SAML path reaches a logged-in session without the MFA stage that the password flow required.

For I3 flow-coherence interpretation, authentik documents that flow execution context is independent per execution and that stage/policy evaluation timing can differ ('Evaluate when flow is planned' vs 'Evaluate when stage is run'). Do not flag a bug merely because an admin changed source/flow configuration between two separate logins. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same logical request/session state, not a legitimate re-evaluation under changed configuration.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier authentik receives from the upstream IdP. The docs state Persistent maps to a hashed ID, Transient maps to session ID, EmailAddress maps to email, and other formats may fall back to persistent identifiers. Keep NameID policy fixed across compared test cases; otherwise identity-collision results may be caused by changing identifier format rather than improper principal binding.

For I4 email-binding collision tests, explicitly choose a NameID policy that is distinct from email when you want to test whether authentik collapses identities by email. If NameID itself is configured as EmailAddress, then NameID=email and email-attribute collisions are not distinguishable.

For I4 cross-protocol or source-stage tests, note that authentik's Source stage resumes the original flow after external authentication and warns that source authentication/enrollment flows must not contain a User Login stage. If a source flow directly logs in the user, identity-binding results can be confounded by flow design rather than source mapping behavior.

For I5 audience/conditions tests, send assertions to the SAML source ACS and vary Conditions/AudienceRestriction in the assertion itself. The docs define the ACS as the assertion consumer and describe SAML assertions as being consumed there. Missing Conditions or wrong Audience must be tested at assertion-consumption time, not against provider metadata endpoints.

NameID values are not stable across all policies by default. authentik documents that EmailAddress NameID uses the user's email and warns users may freely change email addresses; Transient uses the session ID; x509 Subject and Windows may fall back to the persistent identifier if attributes are absent. Never assume NameID is immutable unless the source/provider is explicitly configured for a stable persistent mapping.

For all SAML login tests against authentik as SP, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and then POST the forged SAMLResponse to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with a matching InResponseTo/RelayState. authentik documents SP-initiated SSO and the ACS endpoint; sending an unsolicited fabricated response without first starting the flow will be rejected for flow-state reasons rather than the security property under test.
saml.source: SAML Source docs; ACS URL and SP-initiated flow terminology

saml.constraint: For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish authentik's two SAML roles. The documented SAML provider pages describe authentik acting as IdP for downstream SPs, while the SAML source docs describe authentik acting as SP consuming upstream assertions. Only the SAML source/ACS path is relevant for saml_login in this profile; do NOT infer provider-side signature settings as source-side validation controls.
saml.source: SAML Provider docs vs SAML Source docs

saml.constraint: For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, use the upstream IdP Issuer/Entity ID as the trust anchor. The SAML source configuration explicitly includes an 'Issuer/Entity ID' for the federation and the ACS endpoint under /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. A valid test MUST vary the assertion Issuer against the configured upstream IdP identity, not against authentik's own SP entity ID.

For I1 IdP-initiated scenarios, the fuzzer MUST account for authentik's documented 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' setting. If that setting is enabled, authentik warns that the request is not verified and this may be a security risk. Therefore, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated tests must be separated: a successful unsolicited response when IdP-initiated logins are enabled is not evidence of broken request correlation for SP-initiated flows.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving alternate login paths, authentik's Source stage documentation says source authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage because the source stage appends a dynamic in-memory stage and then resumes the original flow. If a source flow contains User Login, the original flow is not resumed and results are invalid. Do not interpret such misconfiguration as a broker coherence bug.

For I3 timeout/restart scenarios, the Source stage 'Resume timeout' controls how long the suspended flow is saved before return from the external SAML source. If this timeout is exceeded, authentik restarts the suspended flow from the beginning by design. Tests that delay the SAML round-trip beyond this timeout must not be flagged as session-mixup or flow-coherence vulnerabilities.

For I4 principal-binding tests, do NOT assume NameID is the stable authentik-side account key. The docs state NameID policy selection can map to hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email address depending on configuration, and email-based NameID is explicitly warned as mutable. Multi-identity collision tests must vary both NameID and mapped attributes such as email, and must record which source property mappings are in use before concluding that identities collapsed unexpectedly.
saml.source: SAML provider NameID documentation and warning about email-based NameID

saml.constraint: For I4 email-binding collision and cross-protocol merge tests, authentik documentation indicates SAML source/property mappings can map arbitrary upstream attributes into authentik user properties, and users can also authenticate through other sources. Therefore, a merge on email may be by configured mapping rather than an unintended collapse. The fuzzer MUST capture whether email is mapped as the identifying attribute before treating same-email merges as a vulnerability.
saml.source: SAML source property mappings; cross-source authentication model

saml.constraint: For I5 authorization-binding tests that rely on SAML attributes such as groups, remember that authentik property mappings can return non-scalar values and LDAP/source docs note some attributes may be arrays unless flattened. The fuzzer SHOULD test both scalar and list forms for group-like attributes and must not assume a single canonical type when interpreting authorization outcomes.
saml.source: LDAP source property mapping type-carryover docs; provider property mapping model

saml.constraint: The User Login stage uses a duration string where Session duration default 'seconds=0' means the session expires when the browser closes, not an immediately expired session. Do not treat 0 as literal zero-lifetime. Likewise, Stay signed in offset and Remember device only take effect when set above 0. Never assume zero disables authentication itself; it selects browser-session semantics.

The Authenticator Validation stage uses a sentinel threshold where Last validation threshold = 0 means MFA validation is required every time; any non-zero value enables reuse within that window. Do not assume 0 means 'no check'. For freshness-sensitive tests, explicitly keep this at 0 unless you are intentionally testing MFA reuse behavior.

The SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. If enabled, unsolicited SAML responses may be accepted by design. The fuzzer MUST record this setting and MUST NOT report acceptance of unsolicited assertions as a default vulnerability unless the setting is disabled or left at its documented secure default.
